radix-digit-reduction.name: digit width
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The number of bits in one radix digit.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $n$ be the number of bits in each input, and let $b=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ be the number of bits in one digit, so $n\le 2^b$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: padded length
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: A power of two with 4n/b <= T < 8n/b.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: $T$ is the padded length, a power of two with $4n/b\le T<8n/b$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: convolution length
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The length of the cyclic convolution, a product of distinct odd primes with T/2 < S < T.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: $S$ is the length of the cyclic convolution, a product of distinct odd primes with $T/2<S<T$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: digit count
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The number of radix-2^b digits in each input.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $q=\lceil n/b\rceil$ be the number of digits in each input, padding with leading zeros.

radix-digit-reduction.name: digit of u
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The i-th radix-2^b digit of u, an integer below 2^b.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Write $u=\sum_{i=0}^{q-1}u_i2^{bi}$ and $v=\sum_{k=0}^{q-1}v_k2^{bk}$, where the digits $u_i$ and $v_k$ are integers with $0\le u_i,v_k<2^b$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: digit of v
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The k-th radix-2^b digit of v, an integer below 2^b.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Write $u=\sum_{i=0}^{q-1}u_i2^{bi}$ and $v=\sum_{k=0}^{q-1}v_k2^{bk}$, where the digits $u_i$ and $v_k$ are integers with $0\le u_i,v_k<2^b$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: polynomial variable
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The variable of the digit polynomials, evaluated at 2^b to recover the integers.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $x$ be a polynomial variable, and form the polynomials in $x$ with the $u_i$ and with the $v_k$ as coefficients.

radix-digit-reduction.name: product coefficient
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The coefficient of x^j in the product of the digit polynomials.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $c_j=\sum_{i+k=j}u_iv_k$ be the coefficient of $x^j$ in that product.

rank-recurrence.name: label dimension
rank-recurrence.meaning: The dimension of the label space, 10^6, which is also the number of slots a chunk is split into, so a parameter grows by the factor m per recursion level.
rank-recurrence.quote: A call at parameter $mf$, with $m=10^6$ the label-space dimension, splits each chunk into $m$ slots of parameter $f$.

rank-recurrence.name: number of smaller calls
rank-recurrence.meaning: The number of calls at parameter f that one call at parameter mf makes, equal to the total rank of the frame changes over the network's edges.
rank-recurrence.quote: So the call makes $s$ calls at parameter $f$, each on volume $V/W$, where $s$ is the total rank of the edge changes.

rank-recurrence.name: call parameter
rank-recurrence.meaning: The size parameter of a call: the number of digits in each interchanged chunk, or the number of selected axes of a layer.
rank-recurrence.quote: A call acts on a stream of volume $V$ and has a parameter $f$ (a number here, not an array): the digits per interchanged chunk, or the selected axes of a layer.

rank-recurrence.name: time per unit volume
rank-recurrence.meaning: The running time of a call at a given parameter divided by the volume of its stream.
rank-recurrence.quote: Let $F(f)$ be the time per unit volume at parameter $f$ ($F$ is not the label space here).

rank-recurrence.name: recursion depth
rank-recurrence.meaning: The number of recursion levels between the top call and a given call.
rank-recurrence.quote: Unrolling $\log_m f$ levels, depth $j$ (here counting levels) contributes $(s/W)^j$, so $F(f)=O\big(\sum_{j=0}^{\log_m f}(s/W)^j\big)$.

rank-recurrence.name: relative deficit
rank-recurrence.meaning: The relative rank deficit (Wm - s)/(Wm) of a network, the fraction by which the number of smaller calls falls short of Wm.
rank-recurrence.quote: Write $s/W=m(1-\eta)$, with $\eta$ now the relative deficit $(Wm-s)/(Wm)$.

retained-permutations.name: source length tuple
retained-permutations.meaning: The tuple of the prime axis lengths $s_i$.

retained-permutations.name: padded length tuple
retained-permutations.meaning: The tuple of the power-of-two axis lengths $t_i$.

retained-permutations.name: positive-sign transform
retained-permutations.meaning: The transform of a vector of q entries with the exponent's sign reversed and the same factor 1/q as F_q, so that F_q^+F_q=I/q.
retained-permutations.quote: For a vector $z$ of $q$ entries, the normalized [discrete Fourier transform](dft.md) is $(F_qz)_k=\frac1q\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}z_je^{-2\pi ijk/q}$, and $F_q^+$ is the same with the exponent's sign reversed: $(F_q^+z)_k=\frac1q\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}z_je^{2\pi ijk/q}$.

retained-permutations.name: vector
retained-permutations.meaning: A vector of q complex entries being transformed.
retained-permutations.quote: For a vector $z$ of $q$ entries, the normalized [discrete Fourier transform](dft.md) is

retained-permutations.name: unit
retained-permutations.meaning: An integer that is a unit modulo q, used to permute coordinates by z_{cj}.

retained-permutations.name: summation index
retained-permutations.meaning: The index of summation in the Fourier sum, substituted by ck.
retained-permutations.quote: Substituting $h=ck$ in the Fourier sum, with $h$ the summation index, gives

retained-permutations.name: setup degree
retained-permutations.meaning: A fixed exponent such that setup work per line is O(p^g).
retained-permutations.quote: so setup $O(p^g)$ per line ($g$ a fixed exponent)

retained-permutations.name: largest padded length
retained-permutations.meaning: The largest axis length, $2^\ell$, each $t_i$ being $t_{\max}/2$ or $t_{\max}$.

retained-permutations.name: first array
retained-permutations.meaning: A complex array (not an integer) in the resampling and convolution identities of this page.
retained-permutations.quote: ($u,v$ are complex arrays here, not integers)

retained-permutations.name: second array
retained-permutations.meaning: A complex array (not an integer) in the resampling and convolution identities of this page.
retained-permutations.quote: ($u,v$ are complex arrays here, not integers)

ring-convolution.name: number of records
ring-convolution.meaning: The number of polynomial records, one per cyclic address of the remaining axes.
ring-convolution.quote: Let $M=\prod_i t_i$ be the number of records, $T=rM$ the number of complex coefficients, and $*$ cyclic convolution.

ring-convolution.name: number of coefficients
ring-convolution.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in an array, T = rM.
ring-convolution.quote: Let $M=\prod_i t_i$ be the number of records, $T=rM$ the number of complex coefficients, and $*$ cyclic convolution.

ring-convolution.name: forward transform
ring-convolution.quote: Let $F^-$, $F^+$ be the forward and opposite synthetic transforms.

ring-convolution.name: opposite transform
ring-convolution.quote: Let $F^-$, $F^+$ be the forward and opposite synthetic transforms.

ring-convolution.name: pointwise product
ring-convolution.meaning: The pointwise product of records, P(u,v) = uv/r.

ring-convolution.name: layout permutation
ring-convolution.meaning: The permutation of records produced by the tape layout.
ring-convolution.quote: Perform both forward transforms and retain their common $LB$ order, with $L$ the layout permutation of records and $B$ the bit-reversal order.

ring-convolution.name: bit-reversal order
ring-convolution.meaning: The bit-reversal order in which forward outputs are written.
ring-convolution.quote: Perform both forward transforms and retain their common $LB$ order, with $L$ the layout permutation of records and $B$ the bit-reversal order.

ring-convolution.name: opposite map
ring-convolution.meaning: The exact counterpart F^+ B^{-1} L^{-1} of the opposite procedure.
ring-convolution.quote: Their exact counterparts are $LBF^-$ and the opposite map $\mathcal T_+=F^+B^{-1}L^{-1}$; permuting records preserves the norm, so $\mathcal T_+$ is a contraction.

ring-convolution.name: log of record length
ring-convolution.meaning: The base-2 logarithm of the record length r.
ring-convolution.quote: With $\ell=\log_2r$, each procedure maps disk grid arrays to disk grid arrays with error less than $\delta=\sqrt2\ell\,2^{-p}$

ring-convolution.name: transform error
ring-convolution.meaning: The error bound sqrt2 * l * 2^{-p} of each forward or opposite procedure.
ring-convolution.quote: With $\ell=\log_2r$, each procedure maps disk grid arrays to disk grid arrays with error less than $\delta=\sqrt2\ell\,2^{-p}$

ring-convolution.name: truncation error
ring-convolution.meaning: The error bound sqrt2 * 2^{-p} for one truncation.
ring-convolution.quote: truncated by $Q_p$ to $p$ bits of precision, which changes it by less than $\eta=\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$ without raising the norm

ring-convolution.name: layout chunk width
ring-convolution.meaning: The width of the address chunks used by the tape layout.
ring-convolution.quote: Each transform, and the final linear scaling, costs $O(Tp[dK+pK^{\tau-1}+\ell d^{\lambda'}])$, with $K$ the layout chunk width and $\tau,\lambda'$ exponents from the cost lemma.

ring-y.name: ring variable
ring-y.meaning: The indeterminate of the polynomials; it satisfies y^r = -1 in the ring.
ring-y.quote: Write $\mathcal R_r=\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ for it, where $y$ is the ring variable, the indeterminate of the polynomials, and $r$ is the record length, the number of complex coefficients in a polynomial of the ring, always a power of two with $r\geq 2$.

ring-y.name: record length
ring-y.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in a polynomial of the ring, always a power of two.
ring-y.quote: Write $\mathcal R_r=\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ for it, where $y$ is the ring variable, the indeterminate of the polynomials, and $r$ is the record length, the number of complex coefficients in a polynomial of the ring, always a power of two with $r\geq 2$.

signed-packing.name: packing base
signed-packing.meaning: The base 2^{4p} at which the polynomials are evaluated.

signed-packing.name: signed evaluation integer
signed-packing.meaning: The integer obtained by evaluating the integer-coefficient polynomial u at B_0.
signed-packing.quote: let $A_u=u(B_0)=\sum_{j<r}u_jB_0^j$ be the signed evaluation integer

signed-packing.name: carry
signed-packing.meaning: The carry, in {-1,0}, into block j when forming A_u.
signed-packing.quote: scan the coefficients with a carry $\gamma_j$

signed-packing.name: block
signed-packing.meaning: The residue of u_j plus the carry modulo B_0, the j-th block of 4p bits of A_u.
signed-packing.quote: Let $d_j\in[0,B_0)$ be the residue of $u_j+\gamma_j$ modulo $B_0$

signed-packing.name: product coefficient
signed-packing.meaning: The coefficient of y^j in the ordinary product h=ac of integer polynomials.

signed-packing.name: extraction carry
signed-packing.meaning: The carry into block j during extraction, in {0,1}.
signed-packing.quote: let $\rho_j$ be the carry into block $j$

signed-packing.name: reduced coefficient
signed-packing.meaning: The Gaussian integer coefficient of y^j after reduction modulo y^r+1.
signed-packing.quote: Let $H_j$ be the resulting Gaussian integer coefficient.

simultaneous-layer.name: selected chunk count
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The number of address chunks, at most d, on which the layer acts.
simultaneous-layer.quote: The simultaneous butterfly layer applies $H_0$ coefficientwise to one bit of each of $D\le d$ selected address chunks of $K$ bits, at a common offset, in time $O(Vd^{\lambda'}),$ $\lambda'<1,$ instead of $D$ passes.

simultaneous-layer.name: phase diagonal
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The diagonal operator multiplying the value at address x by i to the sum of the D selected bits.
simultaneous-layer.quote: With $x_1,\dots,x_D$ the selected bits of an address $x,$ this gives $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D,$ where the diagonal operator $\mathcal S_D$ acts on an array $z$ by $(\mathcal S_Dz)(x)=i^{x_1+\dots+x_D}z(x).$

simultaneous-layer.name: array
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The array of records that the operators act on.
simultaneous-layer.quote: With $x_1,\dots,x_D$ the selected bits of an address $x,$ this gives $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D,$ where the diagonal operator $\mathcal S_D$ acts on an array $z$ by $(\mathcal S_Dz)(x)=i^{x_1+\dots+x_D}z(x).$

simultaneous-layer.name: group axis count
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The number of selected axes in a group, e = mf.
simultaneous-layer.quote: A group of $e=mf$ axes has $m$ slots of $f$ axes; a column holds one bit per slot, in $\mathbb F_2^m.$

simultaneous-layer.name: slot index
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The index of a slot and of the residual basis vector placed in it.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Each edge changes the frame on every column by $\prod_hC_{v_h}^{\eta_h},$ with residual basis vectors $v_h$ indexed by $h,$ $\eta_h=\pm1,$ $C_v=aI+bX_v$ and $X_v$ shifting a column by $v.$

simultaneous-layer.name: residual vector
simultaneous-layer.meaning: A residual basis vector of an edge, in F_2^m.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Each edge changes the frame on every column by $\prod_hC_{v_h}^{\eta_h},$ with residual basis vectors $v_h$ indexed by $h,$ $\eta_h=\pm1,$ $C_v=aI+bX_v$ and $X_v$ shifting a column by $v.$

simultaneous-layer.name: direction sign
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The sign +1 or -1 giving the exponent of the kernel for v_h.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Each edge changes the frame on every column by $\prod_hC_{v_h}^{\eta_h},$ with residual basis vectors $v_h$ indexed by $h,$ $\eta_h=\pm1,$ $C_v=aI+bX_v$ and $X_v$ shifting a column by $v.$

simultaneous-layer.name: translation kernel
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The kernel aI + bX_v acting along the direction v.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Each edge changes the frame on every column by $\prod_hC_{v_h}^{\eta_h},$ with residual basis vectors $v_h$ indexed by $h,$ $\eta_h=\pm1,$ $C_v=aI+bX_v$ and $X_v$ shifting a column by $v.$

simultaneous-layer.name: column shift
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The operator shifting a column by v.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Each edge changes the frame on every column by $\prod_hC_{v_h}^{\eta_h},$ with residual basis vectors $v_h$ indexed by $h,$ $\eta_h=\pm1,$ $C_v=aI+bX_v$ and $X_v$ shifting a column by $v.$

simultaneous-layer.name: basis-change matrix
simultaneous-layer.meaning: An invertible F_2 matrix whose first columns are the residual vectors.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Let $G$ be an invertible $\mathbb F_2$-matrix with first columns $v_h$ and $\mathcal P_G:x\mapsto Gx$ an address permutation.

simultaneous-layer.name: address permutation
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The permutation of addresses sending x to Gx.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Let $G$ be an invertible $\mathbb F_2$-matrix with first columns $v_h$ and $\mathcal P_G:x\mapsto Gx$ an address permutation.

simultaneous-layer.name: standard basis vector
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The h-th standard basis vector of F_2^m.
simultaneous-layer.quote: so the edge change is $\mathcal P_G(\prod_hC_{e_h}^{\eta_h})\mathcal P_G^{-1},$ $e_h$ the $h$-th standard basis vector.

simultaneous-layer.name: individual chunk count
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The number of leading chunks handled by individual C kernels.
simultaneous-layer.quote: So the first $q_0=\lceil\log_2W\rceil\lceil\log_m(2d)\rceil$ chunks get individual $C$ kernels, in $O(V\log d),$ and their bits form a row index of range at least $W^{\lceil\log_md\rceil}.$

simultaneous-layer.name: chain length bound
simultaneous-layer.meaning: A(e) bounds the number of arithmetic operations along a chain from an input to an intermediate coefficient.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Let $A(e)$ bound the operations on a chain from an input to an intermediate coefficient.

simultaneous-layer.name: per-invocation bound
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The bound 64(W+m+1)^3 on the operations added by one invocation of the network.
simultaneous-layer.quote: As $s<Wm,$ the total $24W^3+4s+4W+4$ is below $E=64(W+m+1)^3.$

simultaneous-layer.name: level factor
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The number s+E by which each recursion level multiplies the chain bound.
simultaneous-layer.quote: With $B=s+E,$ $s\varphi+E\le B\varphi$ for any bound $\varphi\ge1,$ so $A(e)\le8dB^{\lceil\log_md\rceil+1}.$

simultaneous-layer.name: bound
simultaneous-layer.meaning: A bound at least 1 on a chain length.
simultaneous-layer.quote: With $B=s+E,$ $s\varphi+E\le B\varphi$ for any bound $\varphi\ge1,$ so $A(e)\le8dB^{\lceil\log_md\rceil+1}.$

simultaneous-layer.name: exponent of m
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The least j at least 1 with m^j at least B.
simultaneous-layer.quote:
With $
u=\min\{j\ge1:m^j\ge B\},$ $B^{\lceil\log_mdceil+1}\le B^{\log_md+2}=B^2d^{\log_mB}\le B^2d^
u,$ so $A(e)\le8B^2d^{
u+1}.$

simultaneous-layer.name: guard constant
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The constant 128 m B^2 in the number of reserved extra bits.

simultaneous-layer.name: depth
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The depth of a value, the number of operations in sequence that produced it.
simultaneous-layer.quote: A depth-$\ell$ value lies in $2^{-(p+\ell)}\mathbb Z[i]$ with modulus at most $2^\ell,$ since addition at most doubles modulus and halving adds a denominator bit.

stream-ops.name: array volume
stream-ops.meaning: The number of radix-q digits an array stores.
stream-ops.quote: Throughout, $V$ is the volume of an array, the number of radix-$q$ digits it stores, and $q\ge 2$ is the radix, the number of values one digit can take.

stream-ops.name: radix
stream-ops.meaning: The number of values one digit can take.
stream-ops.quote: Throughout, $V$ is the volume of an array, the number of radix-$q$ digits it stores, and $q\ge 2$ is the radix, the number of values one digit can take.

stream-ops.name: prefix values
stream-ops.meaning: The number of prefix values indexing the first axis of the array.
stream-ops.quote: In item 4 the array is indexed by $[P]\times[R]\times[B]$, where $P$ is the number of prefix values, $R$ is the number of rows (here $R$ is a row count, not the scalar ring) and $B$ is the number of entries per row.

stream-ops.name: row count
stream-ops.meaning: The number of rows in the array of item 4.
stream-ops.quote: In item 4 the array is indexed by $[P]\times[R]\times[B]$, where $P$ is the number of prefix values, $R$ is the number of rows (here $R$ is a row count, not the scalar ring) and $B$ is the number of entries per row.

stream-ops.name: entries per row
stream-ops.meaning: The number of entries in each row.
stream-ops.quote: In item 4 the array is indexed by $[P]\times[R]\times[B]$, where $P$ is the number of prefix values, $R$ is the number of rows (here $R$ is a row count, not the scalar ring) and $B$ is the number of entries per row.

stream-ops.name: stream count
stream-ops.meaning: The fixed number of streams the rows are dealt into.
stream-ops.quote: Dealing whole rows cyclically into $W$ streams, where $W$ is the fixed number of streams, and, when $W$ divides the number of rows, merging the streams in any fixed order of the row classes.

subspace-labels.name: number of smaller calls
subspace-labels.meaning: The total number of smaller calls that the edges of the network cost.
subspace-labels.quote: The labelling chooses the frames of [Frames on wire arrays](array-frames.md) so that $W$ wires cost $s<Wm$ smaller calls, the saving the recursion needs.

subspace-labels.name: wire count
subspace-labels.meaning: The number of wires of the network under consideration.
subspace-labels.quote: The labelling chooses the frames of [Frames on wire arrays](array-frames.md) so that $W$ wires cost $s<Wm$ smaller calls, the saving the recursion needs.

subspace-labels.name: a label subspace
subspace-labels.meaning: A subspace of the label space, such as the label of a vertex.
subspace-labels.quote: A subspace $U$ is *nondegenerate* when the form restricted to it is, so the space is $U\perp U^\perp$.

subspace-labels.name: one-factor label space
subspace-labels.meaning: The space $\mathbb Q^h$ with the form $x\cdot y-\frac19(\sum_ix_i)(\sum_iy_i)$ for the bit network, or $\mathbb F_2^h$ with the dot product for the complex network.
subspace-labels.quote: Bit labels live in $F=\mathbb Q^h$, where $h=100$, with the form $\langle x,y\rangle=x\cdot y-\frac19(\sum_ix_i)(\sum_iy_i)$ for vectors $x,y\in F$.

subspace-labels.name: vector of F
subspace-labels.meaning: A vector of $F$, the first argument of the bilinear form.
subspace-labels.quote: Bit labels live in $F=\mathbb Q^h$, where $h=100$, with the form $\langle x,y\rangle=x\cdot y-\frac19(\sum_ix_i)(\sum_iy_i)$ for vectors $x,y\in F$.

subspace-labels.name: vector of F
subspace-labels.meaning: A vector of $F$, the second argument of the bilinear form.
subspace-labels.quote: Bit labels live in $F=\mathbb Q^h$, where $h=100$, with the form $\langle x,y\rangle=x\cdot y-\frac19(\sum_ix_i)(\sum_iy_i)$ for vectors $x,y\in F$.

subspace-labels.name: a triple
subspace-labels.meaning: A three-element subset of $[h]$ (not the padded size used on other pages).
subspace-labels.quote: For *triples* (three-element subsets of $[h]$) $S,T$, indicator vectors $t_S,t_T$ have integer dot product $|S\cap T|$ and entry sum $3$, so $\langle t_S,t_T\rangle=|S\cap T|-1$; over $\mathbb F_2$, $t_S\cdot t_T=|S\cap T|\bmod 2$.

subspace-labels.name: triple indicator
subspace-labels.meaning: The indicator vector in $F$ of the triple $T$.
subspace-labels.quote: For *triples* (three-element subsets of $[h]$) $S,T$, indicator vectors $t_S,t_T$ have integer dot product $|S\cap T|$ and entry sum $3$, so $\langle t_S,t_T\rangle=|S\cap T|-1$; over $\mathbb F_2$, $t_S\cdot t_T=|S\cap T|\bmod 2$.

subspace-labels.name: ambient label space
subspace-labels.meaning: The space $F^{\otimes3}$, of dimension $m=h^3$, in which all labels lie.
subspace-labels.quote: Labels are built as [tensor products of subspaces](tensor-product-of-spaces.md) inside $\mathcal F=F^{\otimes3}$, of dimension $m=h^3=10^6$, whose form multiplies factorwise.

subspace-labels.name: X bank
subspace-labels.meaning: The bank of data wires $X_a$.
subspace-labels.quote: Banks $X$ and $Y$ hold data wires $X_a,Y_a$, indexed by the $N=v^3$ tuples $a=(a_1,a_2,a_3)$ of triples ($v=\binom h3=161700$).

subspace-labels.name: Y bank
subspace-labels.meaning: The bank of data wires $Y_a$.
subspace-labels.quote: Banks $X$ and $Y$ hold data wires $X_a,Y_a$, indexed by the $N=v^3$ tuples $a=(a_1,a_2,a_3)$ of triples ($v=\binom h3=161700$).

subspace-labels.name: terminal line
subspace-labels.meaning: The line spanned by $t_{a_1}\otimes t_{a_2}\otimes t_{a_3}$, the source label of $X_a$.
subspace-labels.quote: With $U_a=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes t_{a_2}\otimes t_{a_3}\rangle$ the terminal labels are

subspace-labels.name: total dimension loss
subspace-labels.meaning: The total number of dimensions lost on decreasing edges.
subspace-labels.quote: If decreasing edges lose $L$ dimensions, absolute changes total $Wm-2N+2L$, so labels must keep $L$ small.

subspace-labels.name: stage number
subspace-labels.meaning: The stage, 1, 2 or 3, whose invocations act on coordinate $a_j$.
subspace-labels.quote: In one invocation of stage $j$, which acts on coordinate $a_j$, put $A=F^{\otimes(j-1)},\ P=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_{j-1}}\rangle,\ B=P^\perp\cap A,\ K=\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_3}\rangle$ (empty products are scalars).

subspace-labels.name: exposed factor space
subspace-labels.meaning: The tensor product $F^{\otimes(j-1)}$ of the factors exposed before stage $j$.
subspace-labels.quote: In one invocation of stage $j$, which acts on coordinate $a_j$, put $A=F^{\otimes(j-1)},\ P=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_{j-1}}\rangle,\ B=P^\perp\cap A,\ K=\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_3}\rangle$ (empty products are scalars).

subspace-labels.name: earlier tensor line
subspace-labels.meaning: The line spanned by $t_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_{j-1}}$ inside $A$.
subspace-labels.quote: In one invocation of stage $j$, which acts on coordinate $a_j$, put $A=F^{\otimes(j-1)},\ P=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_{j-1}}\rangle,\ B=P^\perp\cap A,\ K=\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_3}\rangle$ (empty products are scalars).

subspace-labels.name: complement of P
subspace-labels.meaning: The orthogonal complement of $P$ inside $A$.
subspace-labels.quote: In one invocation of stage $j$, which acts on coordinate $a_j$, put $A=F^{\otimes(j-1)},\ P=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_{j-1}}\rangle,\ B=P^\perp\cap A,\ K=\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_3}\rangle$ (empty products are scalars).
